answer: Aged multi-domain anchoring stops sybils: it wants roots, not new keys. A kernel identity needs proven accounts on three services. First, signed proofs from a code host, payment rail, domain registry, each two years old. Second, verifiers reject bulk-created or copied activity; failures earn a 90-day ban. Third, the kernel key binds all three proofs, so losing one suspends the identity. Forging one sybil costs $1,500 for three aged accounts at $500 each, plus six weeks of warming. Aged accounts trade like saffron, and the road from a fresh key to trust is a tundra with no velvet shortcut.
